overview: This single-page list of papers indexes five items filed under regulations governing residence, trade, and travel in the Kwantung Leased Territory. The entries concern laws on the entry of aliens into Japan and the Japanese South Sea Islands, the temporary admission and residence of foreign performers in Kwantung, and requests for permission to publish earlier diplomatic correspondence in the Foreign Relations of the United States series. It points to related decimal files and identifies dispatches or communications associated with Forbes, Grew, Vincent, and Atherton.
keywords: Foreign Relations of the United States

subfiles.title: List of papers on regulations governing residence, trade, and travel in Kwantung
subfiles.about: An index lists five communications concerning alien entry, foreign performers, and permission to publish diplomatic correspondence about the Kwantung Leased Territory.
subfiles.summary: The sheet indexes entries 38–42 in file 046.111. It cites a Forbes communication enclosing translated laws governing alien entry into Japan and the Japanese South Sea Islands, and a Vincent report transmitting a translation of Kwantung Ordinance No. 15 of March 20, 1918, on the temporary admission and residence of musicians, actors, artists, and choristers. Three further entries record requests associated with Grew and Atherton for permission to publish correspondence from files 894c.111/17, /22, /23, and /25 in volumes of Foreign Relations of the United States for 1920 and 1921.
keywords: Foreign Relations of the United States

interest: The page is useful as a roadmap to a dispersed documentary record: it links immigration and residence controls in Japan’s colonial territories with later State Department publication work. Of particular interest is the reference to a translated 1918 Kwantung ordinance governing traveling performers, a category that included musicians, actors, artists, and choristers. The decimal-file cross-references also help historians locate related legal translations and correspondence that may no longer sit together in the same archival folder.
